title: Contextualizing Hate Speech Classifiers with Post-hoc Explanation

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring model over-sensitivity to racial and ethnic identifiers (e.g., 'black', 'white', 'mexican', 'africans') by computing post-hoc feature importance via the Sampling and Occlusion (SOC) algorithm and evaluating false positive rates on an adversarial, non-hateful dataset of New York Times articles containing these terms.

Measuring model over-sensitivity to religious identifiers (e.g., 'muslim', 'jew', 'islamic') by computing post-hoc feature importance via the Sampling and Occlusion (SOC) algorithm and tracking false positive rates on an adversarial dataset devoid of hate speech.

Measuring model over-sensitivity to sexual orientation and gender identity terms (e.g., 'gay', 'lesbian', 'homosexual', 'transgender') using the Sampling and Occlusion (SOC) feature attribution algorithm and testing on an adversarial text corpus to measure false positive rates.

Measuring model over-sensitivity to gender identifiers (e.g., 'women', 'woman') using the Sampling and Occlusion (SOC) explanation algorithm to determine feature weight, and evaluating predictive bias via false positives on an out-of-domain, non-hateful dataset.
